name: Pizza comparison
seoDesc: Pizza comparison: work out area of a small pizza from the diameter and number of pizzas. A free food calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: The Pizza comparison calculator turns the diameter, number of pizzas and more into area of a small pizza. It suits portioning, timing or nutrition. Editing anything puts the results away until the next press of Calculate — change one value at a time and the updated answer tells you what that value was worth.

sections.title: How does the Pizza comparison calculator work?
sections.html:
The Pizza comparison calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports area of a small pizza in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the diameter (Smaller pizza), number of pizzas (Smaller pizza), the price and the price difference.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Pizza comparison calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Area of a small pizza=(1 ÷ 4) × PI × (diameter ^ 2)
Diameter=(4000 ÷ 20943951) × the square root of (34906585) × the square root of (area of a large pizza)
Area of a small pizza=total area of the small pizzas ÷ number of pizzas
Number of pizzas=total area of the large pizzas ÷ area of a large pizza
Area difference=total area of the large pizzas ÷ total area of the small pizzas
Price per pizza=total price ÷ number of pizzas

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Length, opening in centimeters
  • Currency, opening in US Dollar
  • Currency, opening in US Dollar
  • Length, opening in centimeters
  • Currency, opening in US Dollar

  • %, opening in percent
  • Area, opening in square centimeters

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Pizza comparison calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Checking portions before you shop
  • Scaling a recipe up or down
  • Working out timing so everything finishes together
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the diameter, number of pizzas and the price — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Pizza comparison calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns area of a small pizza, derived from the diameter, number of pizzas and the price. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Pizza comparison calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the diameter, number of pizzas, the price and the price difference, which is 6 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter diameter (Smaller pizza) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Diameter (Smaller pizza) opens in centimeters and the chip beside it offers 34 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: Is the Pizza comparison calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
